findings.summary: I checked the delta and found nothing blocking. HEAD is c995a8c8. The census tool, the tests and historical-compatibility.md match the SHA-256 values given in the brief. package.json changes only security:history:check: it still runs verify-historical-compatibility.mjs and historical-compatibility.test.mjs, and adds the census run and the census test file. The tool reports structure only: it has no resolver or waiver path, and authenticatedOrigin is false everywhere.

All seven earlier source and docs defects are fixed. (1) The CLI check now uses import.meta.main, or compares realpaths on both sides, and has a test that runs it through an external symlink. (2) Each file now records indexBlobOid, worktreeBlobOid (computed in the repo's Git object format) and worktreeMatchesIndex, with a test for a changed worktree. (3) The report states citationGrammar: expression, flags, the 3–4 digit range, UTF-16 code-unit offsets, and its limits; a test covers emoji and grammar edge cases. (4) The selector now uses a case-insensitive .json check without a regex, so uppercase-extension and newline paths are kept. (5) A UTF-8 BOM is refused with UTF8_BOM_REFUSED. (6) Provider errors now separate ENOENT/source-unavailable, MANIFEST_SHAPE_INVALID and observation-error with a specific reason code. (7) Provider paths are package-relative; v2 contains no /Volumes or /Users paths.

The v2 data matches the documented figures. working-census-v2.json has complete=true and no errors, 122 files (121 schemas plus manifest.json), 138 occurrences and 47 unique IDs. There are 96 annotation-value and 42 data-keyword-value rows. All six ADR-014 rows sit under the root examples keyword at the six pointers listed in the doc. 121 files are byte-equal to the installed provider files; manifest.json is source-unavailable (ENOENT). In custody-v2, all 122 baseComparisons are byteEqual and worktreeMatchesIndex true, and the hashes of the six capture files match the bytes on disk.

The v1 files are byte-exact. On-disk hashes of working-census.json, inspector-report.json, inspector-tests.stdout/stderr, inspector-test-lint.log, independent-review.json and independent-review.bridge.json match custody.json. The Inspector v2 streams show 23 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip. The baseline red run shows 22 tests: 17 pass and 5 fail, and the failures are caused by the five repaired defects. The doc keeps the native findings, the 14 missing round records, R-0017's mutation, the prose ADR gap and R-0036's sealed status. It correctly calls this delta review pending.

inspector-review-report-v2.json still lists /tmp/... paths for its stdout/stderr. Custody is intact, because custody-v2 captureFiles maps each /tmp source to the repo copy and its hash. A reader of the report alone could still be misled; noting the repo copies would help.

security:history:check now prints the whole census JSON to stdout on every run (about 290 KB on the real repo). It also passes when worktree files differ from the index (worktreeMatchesIndex=false), because complete only covers the declared tracked population. That matches the documented basis, but the gate will not catch locally modified schema bytes. A summary-only mode or redirecting the output may be worth it before CI wiring.

Several refusal paths still have no tests: TRACKED_POPULATION_CHANGED, UNMERGED_INPUT (stage≠0), a gitlink (mode 160000) refused as TRACKED_INPUT_NOT_REGULAR, and the dependencies and items-array context branches. Reading the code, the guards look correct.
